title: Field hearthline notes and feature-claim map - 2025-11-03
summary: Compact synthesis of field interviews (9 customers) with prioritized feature claims and low-effort mitigation ideas. Focus: predictable latency, KV caching clarity, and per-route cost visibility.
content:
Why this note exists:
- Quick capture from last two weeks of CS field calls, remote pairing sessions, and a short survey of heavy inference accounts. Objective: consolidate recurring asks into a small set of implementable claims and flag risk areas we should treat as high-visibility.

Method and scope:
- Interviews: 9 customers (3 enterprise SaaS, 4 AI-native startups, 2 platform teams).
- Data sources: support threads, latency dashboards, a short sample of token-level billing traces, and two on-call postmortems.
- Lens: production pain points that block adoption or cause escalation (latency spikes, cost surprises, deployment model mismatch).

Top recurring customer claims (ranked by frequency + impact):
1) "Opaque cost divergence for streaming vs batch" (8/9 mentions)
   - Claim: Customers are surprised that streaming endpoints (low-latency) can bill materially more per-interaction than batched generation; hard to model costs across experiment-to-prod.
   - Example quote: "We budget per-agent call, but the streaming shape blew our numbers by 3x in one week."
   - Immediate mitigation: add a per-route cost simulator in console that projects cost for streaming vs batch using a simple token distribution input (low-effort, product spike).

2) "KV cache semantics unclear across private/dedicated" (7/9 mentions)
   - Claim: Engineers unsure when prefix caching is preserved vs invalidated across model rollouts and autoscaling events. Leads to accidental cache misses and latency regressions.
   - Symptoms: observed pattern of cold-cache latency spikes after canary rollouts; customers attribute to infra but root cause often cache eviction or placement.
   - Ask: clearer docs + a `cache-debug` flag in API responses indicating hit/miss and eviction reason (TTL / memory pressure / model switch).

3) "Per-token latency variance during long-lived streams" (6/9)
   - Claim: For streaming chat sessions with longer histories, tail latency increases unpredictably; customers see timeouts or truncated ingest.
   - Quick hypothesis: KV cache compaction and attention kernel fallback for long seqs causing variable scheduling.
   - Probe: run a smoke suite that replays 3 long histories across dedicated pools and gather kernel selection logs.

4) "Rollout visibility for model variants" (5/9)
   - Claim: Platform teams want richer telemetry on which model variant served which request (including quantization/bit-width details) to correlate quality/regression signals.
   - Short-term ask: include variant metadata in sampling logs and rollout dashboards.

Micro-vignettes (raw field snippets):
- "We turned on caching, thought it would save us tokens, but latency got worse when traffic spiked — what's the tradeoff?" (mid-market search vendor)
- "During a demo, the bot went silent for 12s mid-response; client demo = ruined. We can't rely on best-effort guarantees." (SaaS PM)

Feature-claim map (compact, with proposed effort bands)
- A: Console cost simulator for streaming vs batch (effort: small) -> product spike + design -> ship MVP in 4 weeks.
- B: `cache-debug` flag / hit-miss telemetry in API responses (effort: medium) -> engineering + SDK bump -> ship in 6-8 weeks.
- C: Tail-latency smoke suite + kernel telemetry (effort: medium) -> infra + runtime team -> 3-week spike then 4-week rollout.
- D: Model-variant sampling metadata in rollout dashboards (effort: small) -> add fields to logs + dashboard filter -> 2-3 weeks.

Low-effort mitigations we can do today:
- Add a short KB article "How caching interacts with rollouts and autoscaling" and link it in onboarding emails (owner: CS content, due: next Tue).
- Provide customers a quick-run checklist for demos: use pinned model variant + disable autoscale + pre-warm cache (one-pager we can email).
- Expose a temporary Beta metric for streaming cost-per-request in console (approximation using sampled token-lengths).

Open questions / uncertainties:
- How often do canary rollouts actually force cache invalidation vs just warm-up? Need a small instrumentation spike to tag rollout events with cache stats.
- Which kernel fallback scenarios are most common on A100 vs older cards? (ask serving-runtime to add card-type to trace samples).

Suggested next actions (owners + short timeline):
- Product: scope console cost-sim spike (Ava + Miguel) - define inputs and mockups by 2025-11-10.
- Eng (runtime): instrument cache hit/miss with rollout events and surface a small event stream for CS (Ethan) - spike 2 weeks.
- CS: draft demo-checklist and KB article + outreach to the 9 customers with a 1:1 note and mitigation tips (Sofia) - deliver in 5 business days.

Risks to call out to leadership:
- If we don't reduce cost-visibility friction, several small customers will throttle usage or pause expansion while they rebuild cost models in-house.
- Experiential risk: demo-time tail latency events are high leverage and can materially slow enterprise adoption.

Appendix: quick references and snippets
- Sample billing trace (redacted) attached in linked_artifacts: linear/abc-402.
- Slack thread: #cs-field-hearthline 2025-10-22 contains raw transcripts and quotes.

Notes to self:
- Push follow-up instrumentation tickets into the runtime team's triage board; mark as high-visibility.
- Re-run this synthesis after engineering spike and update owners column.

End of note.
